plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis 'Somei-Yoshino'
plants.description: Bare branches turn into clouds of blush-white blossoms. Thousands of five-petaled flowers open before the leaves, so each tree looks like a drift of pale pink snow. Petals fall in soft showers that carpet parks, riverbanks and temple grounds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April in central Japan. In Tokyo, blooming began on March 19 in 2026 and reached full bloom by March 28. Timing shifts a few days earlier or later each year with spring temperatures.
plants.location: Tokyo and other lowland cities in central and western Japan, including Kyoto, Kofu and Gifu. The tree is also planted widely in temperate parks around the world.
plants.funFact: Nearly all Somei-Yoshino trees are clones, grafted from cuttings of a single original tree. That is why whole cities' worth of trees open within days of each other, and why Japan's weather agency can track the national 'cherry blossom front' using a few sample trees.
